overview: The two halves of breathing, driven by opposite changes in the volume and pressure of the chest cavity.
genZNote: Inspiration: chest expands, air rushes in. Expiration: chest shrinks, air gets pushed out.

aspects.label: Diaphragm Movement
aspects.valueA: Diaphragm contracts and flattens, increasing thoracic volume.
aspects.valueB: Diaphragm relaxes and domes upward, decreasing thoracic volume.

aspects.label: Pressure Change
aspects.valueA: Lung pressure drops below atmospheric pressure, drawing air in.
aspects.valueB: Lung pressure rises above atmospheric pressure, pushing air out.

aspects.label: Active or Passive?
aspects.valueA: An active process, requiring muscle contraction.
aspects.valueB: Usually a passive process at rest, driven by elastic recoil of the lungs.

overlay.examHighYieldNote: Forced expiration (like during exercise) becomes an active process, using the internal intercostal and abdominal muscles.
overlay.memoryTrick: Inspiration = 'in' = breathing in. Expiration = 'ex/exit' = breathing out.
overlay.commonMisconception: Normal quiet expiration is passive, not muscle-driven — only forced/heavy expiration actively recruits muscles.
